name: Alma vs Lyra Health
title: Alma vs Lyra Health: Individual vs Enterprise Mental Health Platforms
description: Compare Alma (individual therapist platform) vs Lyra Health (enterprise workforce solution). Understand which platform serves your needs - private practice or employer-sponsored care.

summary.bottom_line: Alma and Lyra Health serve entirely different markets. Alma is a $95-125/month platform for independent therapists to accept insurance. Lyra Health is an enterprise workforce mental health solution for employers (custom PEPM pricing) serving 20M+ people globally. Individual clinicians join Alma; organizations contract with Lyra.

key_differences.scale: Alma: Not disclosed | Lyra: 20M+ people, 90+ countries
key_differences.use_case: Alma: Private practice insurance | Lyra: Workforce mental health benefit
key_differences.clinical_model: Alma: Provider platform | Lyra: End-to-end care delivery

rows.entity_b: Provider matching, Lyra AI conversational tool

sections.heading: Fundamentally Different Platforms
sections.content: Alma and Lyra Health address different sides of the mental health ecosystem. Alma helps individual therapists build private practices by handling insurance credentialing and billing. Lyra Health provides enterprise workforce mental health benefits to employers, offering employees access to vetted therapists, coaches, and psychiatrists. If you're a therapist, you'd join Alma; if you're an HR leader, you'd contract with Lyra.

sections.heading: Pricing Models
sections.content: Alma charges therapists $95/month (annual) or $125/month for credentialing, EHR, AI notes, and billing services. Lyra Health uses custom per-employee-per-month (PEPM) pricing negotiated with employers, with setup costs ranging from $5,000 to over $50,000. Lyra's 3:1 ROI means every $1 invested saves $3.04 in healthcare costs.

sections.heading: Service Differences
sections.content: Alma is a practice infrastructure platform: credentialing, claims submission, EHR, AI documentation (Note Assist), and peer community. Lyra is an end-to-end care delivery system: therapy, coaching, medication management, digital CBT tools, Lyra AI for mild symptoms, and comprehensive HR analytics through Lyra Empower. Both use AI, but for different purposes.

sections.heading: Which Is Right for You?
sections.content: The choice depends on who you are:

recommendations.when: You're an independent therapist wanting to accept insurance and need practice management tools.
You're an employer (500+ employees) seeking comprehensive workforce mental health benefits with proven ROI.
Therapists can potentially join Alma for their private practice while also being part of Lyra's provider network for employer clients.

faqs.q: Can a therapist use both Alma and Lyra Health?
faqs.a: Potentially yes - you could use Alma for your private practice insurance credentialing while also being a provider in Lyra's network to see employer-sponsored clients. These serve different client populations.

faqs.q: Which is better for a small therapy practice?
faqs.a: Alma. Lyra Health is designed for large employers, not individual practices. A small practice would use Alma for insurance credentialing and practice management.

faqs.q: How do Lyra Health's outcomes compare?
faqs.a: Lyra publishes peer-reviewed research showing 3:1 ROI, 2x faster recovery, and 26% reduction in overall healthcare claims. Alma doesn't measure clinical outcomes - it's a practice platform, not a care delivery system.
